name: Build Hybrid Wordlist (Policy Filtering)
description: Trims a large password list down to only candidates that satisfy a known password policy, shrinking the keyspace and attack time. Chain grep -E filters for minimum length, upper, lower, digit, and symbol requirements to match the target's rules.

examples.label: policy filter
examples.command: grep -E '^.{6,}$' names.txt | grep -E '[A-Z]' | grep -E '[a-z]' | grep -E '[0-9]' | grep -E '([!@#$%^&*].*){2,}' > filtered.txt

notes: Filter a big wordlist to match the target's password POLICY (min length, complexity) so you don't waste attempts on candidates that can't be valid. `grep -E` for length/charset rules.

recommended.note: Feed the policy-filtered wordlist into a form attack.

defense.why_it_works: Password policies (minimum length, required character classes) publicly constrain what valid passwords look like. A 14-million entry rockyou.txt wordlist contains mostly short, simple passwords that a policy-enforcing application will immediately reject. Filtering the wordlist through grep/awk to retain only entries that satisfy all policy constraints eliminates ~99% of candidates, leaving only those the application will actually evaluate. This reduces total brute-force attempts by orders of magnitude and focuses effort on policy-compliant, humanly plausible passwords — the exact intersection where real user passwords exist.
defense.prerequisites: Source wordlist (rockyou.txt or similar). Knowledge of the target's password policy (often displayed on registration/login pages, or leaked via error messages). grep/awk on the attacker's system.
defense.impact: Policy-compliant targeted wordlist that dramatically improves brute-force efficiency — fewer attempts, faster results, lower detection footprint. Used to feed Hydra, Medusa, ffuf, or any brute-force tool in the next attack phase.
defense.detection: No network activity — runs locally. Detection only possible in the subsequent brute-force phase.
defense.artifacts: Filtered wordlist file on attacker's disk. No target-side artifacts.
defense.prevention: Displaying password policy on the login page assists attackers in wordlist filtering. Consider not advertising policy details. More importantly: policies alone do not prevent brute-force — lockout, rate limiting, MFA, and monitoring are the effective controls. Use a breach password blocklist (Have I Been Pwned API) to reject known leaked passwords regardless of policy compliance.
defense.evasion: The filtering step runs entirely offline — invisible to all monitoring. Produces a smaller wordlist that generates fewer failed attempts during the attack phase, reducing detection signal.
defense.misconfiguration: Password policies are insufficiently strict: minimum length too short (< 12 chars), no complexity requirement, no history check (allows password reuse), no lockout or too-lenient lockout threshold. Combined with credential reuse across services, a single cracked hash grants access to multiple systems.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak domain password policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# MinPasswordLength:    8    <-- too short
# PasswordHistoryCount: 0    <-- no history, password reuse allowed
# ComplexityEnabled:    False <-- no complexity
# LockoutThreshold:     0    <-- NO lockout

# Local SAM policy (workgroup machines):
# Control Panel -> Local Security Policy -> Account Policies -> Password Policy
# Same weak defaults as above
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong domain password policy:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -MinPasswordLength 14 \
    -PasswordHistoryCount 24 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true \
    -MaxPasswordAge 90.00:00:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5 \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00

# Fine-Grained PSO for privileged accounts (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name PrivilegedPSO \
    -MinPasswordLength 20 -PasswordHistoryCount 48 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true -LockoutThreshold 3 \
    -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject PrivilegedPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Deploy Azure AD Password Protection (blocks common passwords on-prem too)
# Enable Microsoft Entra ID Smart Lockout

variations.label: Policy with symbols
variations.command: grep -E '^.{8,}$' <wordlist> | grep -E '[A-Z]' | grep -E '[a-z]' | grep -E '[0-9]' | grep -E '([!@#$%^&*].*){2,}' > filtered.txt
variations.description: Adds a symbols filter requiring 2+ special characters (!@#$%^&*) on top of the standard length/upper/lower/digit filters. Use when the target policy mandates special characters.
